item.description:

ABNT20 KNHC 030526

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
200 AM EDT Thu Sep 3 2026

For the North Atlantic...Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of America:

Active Systems:
The Weather Prediction Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Depression Edouard, located inland over eastern Texas.

Tropical cyclone formation is not expected during the next 7 days.

$$
Forecaster Pasch

item.title: Summary for Remnants of Edouard (AT5/AL052026)
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)
item.description: ...EDOUARD'S REMNANTS WILL CONTINUE TO PRODUCE HEAVY RAINFALL AND FLOODING THROUGH THURSDAY... As of 4:00 AM CDT Thu Sep 03 the center of Edouard was located near 32.5, -96.5 with movement WNW at 5 mph. The minimum central pressure was 1012 mb with maximum sustained winds of about 25 mph.

item.title: Remnants of Edouard Public Advisory Number 12
item.description: The NHC has issued its final advisory on this system. Public Advisories from the Weather Prediction Center will provide updates as long as the system remains a flood threat. Issued at 400 AM CDT Thu Sep 03 2026

item.title: Tropical Depression Edouard Forecast Discussion Number 11
item.description:
Issued at 1000 PM CDT Wed Sep 02 2026 
493 
WTNT45 KWNH 030311
TCDAT5
 
Tropical Depression Edouard Discussion Number  11
NWS Weather Prediction Center College Park MD   AL052026
1000 PM CDT Wed Sep 02 2026
 
Rainfall forecasts for the United States can always be found at
https://www.wpc.ncep.noaa.gov/qpf/qpf2.shtml
and outlooks of flash flood risks can be found at
https://www.wpc.ncep.noaa.gov/qpf/excessive_rainfall_outlook_ero.php
 
For a list of rainfall observations and wind reports associated
with Edouard, see the companion storm summary at WBCSCCNS5 with the
WMO header ACUS45 KWBC or at the following link:
www.wpc.ncep.noaa.gov/discussions/nfdscc5.html.
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Wind gusts of 30 to 40 mph will continue near the center of
Edouard for the next several hours.
 
2. Heavy rain bands from Edouard will persist over east-central
Texas into Thursday morning before becoming more scattered by midday
Thursday. Flash flooding, including additional significant flash
flooding, is expected over the Piney Woods area of eastern Texas.
Isolated moderate to major river flooding is expected.
